Photograph: Niranjan Shrestha/AP Nepal Flash floods on Nepal-Tibet border leave scores dead and hundreds missing At least 157 people dead and hundreds of tourists among missing after roads, bridges and power plants swept away Nepal-Tibet floods – latest updates Hannah Ellis-Petersen and agencies Wed 26 Aug 2026 14.28 EDT First published on Wed 26 Aug 2026 06.45 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google At least 157 people have been killed and hundreds, including large numbers of foreign tourists, are missing after flash floods ⁠hit the Himalayan border areas of ⁠Nepal and Tibet in China , police have said, with parts of India also at risk. The disaster was caused by a torrent of mud, water and debris that burst from the banks of a river that runs between China and Nepal. Homes, roads, bridges and power plants were swept away in Nepal, ⁠while officials in Tibet said they feared “major casualties”. Authorities issued alerts urging residents in several districts to keep away from the Bhote Koshi, Trishuli and Narayani rivers in Nepal . Officials in Nepal said 403 people, including 341 from foreign countries including India, the US, the UK, Australia, South Korea and Malaysia, had been reported missing in the country. Nepal’s tourism board said more than 100 of those missing were religious tourists from India and the Indian diaspora on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus. At least 62 missing Nepali citizens were among hundreds of locals trekking in Rasuwa, one of the worst hit districts. In Tibet, China’s state broadcaster said at least three people were killed and 265 were missing. View image in fullscreen The aftermath of the flash flood in the Nuwakot district of Nepal. Photograph: Xinhua/Shutterstock Experts were still determining the exact cause of the disaster. The US Geological Survey reported a magnitude-4.4 earthquake in Nepal early Wednesday, near the border with Tibet. It is thought to have triggered a large chunk of ice to snap off from a glacier, which crashed into a mountain valley and caused a sudden downstream surge on the Lhende KholaRiver, a tributary of the Bhote Koshi. Officials said the flooding could get worse because parts of the river remained blocked by ice rocks and debris. Flood alerts were also issued in the Indian states of Bihar and Uttar ​Pradesh, which border Nepal and are downstream of the affected rivers. Police in Nepal said they were still unable to assess the full scale of the damage. Rescuers said helicopters could not land in affected areas of ⁠Syapru Besi and Timure in the mountainous district of Rasuwa until the river waters had receded. Rescue efforts were also hampered by heavy monsoon rains. Footage shows scale of floods in Nepal Images of crumbled homes in ‌the flood waters, floating cars and a ‌metal bridge being washed away, and villages engulfed by water, mud and debris were broadcast on Nepali television. “There could be heavy casualties or loss of property,” ‌said the district administrator, Narendra Pariyar, who urged those living on the banks of the Bhote Koshi to move to higher ground. “There is devastation everywhere we look,” said Tula Bahadur BK, a health worker in Rasuwa. “The settlements next to the river have been completely swept away. Five of my own relatives are missing.” Nepal’s energy ministry said the country’s electricity supplies had been significantly affected, mostly as a result of destroyed hydroelectric plants. Police and military officers joined in Nepal’s rescue effort, the country’s prime minister, Balendra Shah, said. “Instructions have ​been given … to move the people living in ​the lower areas to safer places. People along the river are advised to exercise extra caution ​and remain alert.” The Indian prime minister, Narendra Modi, said he had spoken with Shah and offered Nepal “all possible types of humanitarian assistance”. China’s official Xinhua news agency said the ​flash flood occurred on the Nepal side of the border and cut roads, communications and power links in the Shigatse region. Chinese authorities were conducting large-scale search and rescue operations in the Tibetan border area of Gyirong, according to state broadcaster CCTV. View image in fullscreen Rescuers use a digger to move a survivor of the flash flood to safety in the Nuwakot district of Nepal. Photograph: Prakash Mathema/AFP/Getty Images China’s president, Xi Jinping, urged “all-out” search efforts for the missing and better monitoring and early warning systems to prevent secondary disasters. The Himalayan region, which spans Nepal, India, China and Bhutan, is particularly vulnerable to floods and landslides because it is warming faster than the rest of the world as a result of the climate crisis. Research shows that extreme weather events such as heatwaves and torrential rains have become more frequent. Nepal’s snow-capped mountains had lost close to one-third of their ice in just over 30 years due to global warming, the United Nations said in 2023. Experts have called for greater surveillance and early warning systems across the Himalayan region. Last year, a flood from the Bhote Koshi River killed nine people and washed away a “friendship bridge” linking Nepal and China, disrupting trade and transport for months. Researchers in Kathmandu also found earlier this year that glaciers across the Hindu Kush region were melting at an accelerating rate. Ice loss rates have doubled since 2000. "At my direction, ‌we worked with representatives of Denmark and Greenland to ‌guarantee ​that the United States will FOREVER have the complete ability to do what is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend ​the security of Greenland, and the United States of America," Trump said on Truth Social. The US State Department said the deal bars US adversaries from establishing bases there. "The agreement explicitly guarantees the United States the complete ability to do what it deems is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend the American continent, including permanent access, basing, and overflight rights," a State Department official said. "This agreement guarantees that China and Russia cannot have a base in Greenland, they cannot send troops to Greenland, and the necessary mechanisms are in place to prevent investment in sensitive sectors." In his post, Trump wrote that the US would "immediately" begin developing a larger military presence on the Danish territory. According to a joint statement by the Danish and Greenlandic governments, the United States, Denmark, and Greenland have announced a breakthrough in their dispute over the Arctic island. "I am pleased that there is a prospect of a good agreement for Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark and the United States," Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said in a statement. She added that the deal was "great for NATO and Europe" and recognized "the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom (of Denmark) and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination." The agreement is expected to be signed next week on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. Jens-Frederik Nielsen, the head of Greenland's government, said, "It is gratifying that we are about to enter into an agreement that ensures and strengthens the security of Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark, the United States, and the Western alliance." The deal benefits all three governments and "recognizes Greenland’s interests and our place in the international cooperation," Nielsen added. Since returning to the White House last year, Trump has pressed Denmark to sell Greenland to the United States and even threatened to take it by force, insisting that the island is crucial for US security. Denmark and Greenland have repeatedly stated that the island is not for sale and have condemned reports of the US gathering intelligence there. What should the EU's new Arctic strategy look like? His remarks follow a Danish warning that Moscow could attempt a limited attack on NATO members. by Kyiv Post | Sept. 24, 2026, 11:10 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe (SACEUR) General Alexus G. (Photo by Simon Wohlfahrt / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip NATO allies are increasing their intelligence-sharing as suspected Russian sabotage spreads across Europe. Speaking during a telephone interview with Reuters on Thursday, Supreme Allied Commander Europe (SACEUR) General Alexus Grynkewich urged partners to stay calm about the threat from Moscow, saying that the alliance has the tools it needs to manage the risk. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . “It’s concerning,” Grynkewich said about the recent incidents, while also describing NATO as “the most powerful alliance in history.” Meanwhile, the Kremlin continues rejecting claims about it conducting hybrid operations on NATO territory, while also denying seeking a confrontation with the alliance. Denmark warns of escalation The general’s remarks followed the latest assessment from Denmark’s defense intelligence service, which expects Moscow to step up its hybrid attacks, including sabotage, cyberattacks and a limited ground incursion, against Ukraine’s Western partners in the upcoming months. Advertisement According to Reuters, Danish intelligence also saw a low but growing risk of Russia launching a limited military strike on one or more NATO members, particularly the Baltic states. Other European leaders frequently raise similar alarms. Last week, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that intelligence assessments indicate Russia is planning to strike countries supporting Kyiv , including Poland. In recent months, Russian drone incursions and other hybrid attacks have nearly doubled. Several member states now view them as direct attacks rather than isolated incidents. On Tuesday, President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Moscow could target another EU country with drones, missiles or ground forces in an effort to divide the West and suppress backing for Kyiv. During the UN Security Council on Wednesday, Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski confronted Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov , while also echoing Tusk’s warning that the danger was spreading beyond Ukraine, pointing to strikes near NATO borders and airspace violations. Advertisement “Russia is now bringing the same tactics into Europe,” he said. Grynkewich: ‘Not on my watch’ Although a limited Russian attack on NATO territory is unlikely, it is something that cannot be ruled out completely, Grynkewich told Reuters. “If we proceed from the phase we’re in and we start to see emerging threats, I’m confident that I have the authorities now that I need in order to take actions to deter any aggression against the alliance,” he said. During the telephone call, the general was on his way to a change-of-command ceremony held at NATO headquarters in Norfolk, Virginia, where a command was scheduled to pass from a US Navy vice admiral to a British army general. According to Reuters, the move is a part of a wider reorganization driven by US President Donald Trump’s push for the EU to take greater charge of its own defense. An EU officer is also set to lead NATO’s Joint Force Command in Naples, Italy. The Norfolk command oversees operations in the Arctic and northern Europe and safeguards the supply lines connecting North America and Europe. Grynkewich said Washington would keep offering “critical but more limited capabilities” as the EU assumes a bigger share of the burden. Advertisement Washington has led NATO since 1949. As of recently, Trump consistently threatens to pull the US out of NATO, arguing that the EU has relied on American protection without providing anything in return. A string of incidents Among the incidents that particularly worried him, Grynkewich cited a failed drone attack on Germany’s Leipzig/Halle Airport and a Russian vessel firing flares in the direction of a Danish military helicopter – which Moscow portrayed as the prevention of a Danish “provocation.” On Sept. 16, Russian Defense Minister Andrei Belousov awarded the unnamed commander of the Baltic Fleet corvette Soobrazitelny with the medal “For Combat Distinction.” A Russian Mi-8 military helicopter from the Kaliningrad region crossed into Polish airspace for about 42 seconds on Wednesday. On Thursday, a Russian strike drone flew into Romania from Ukrainian airspace and came down in a forest in Suceava County. NATO fighter jets were unable to intercept it, marking the second day in a row that Russian aircraft entered alliance airspace unchallenged .
